Mateo / team — quick technical constraints from entitlement side:

- Our entitlement keys are provider-agnostic but include a provider tag. We can use a canonical SKU (ACME-CORE) with provider-specific aliases (ACME-CORE-AWS, ACME-CORE-AZ). This keeps downstream billing and analytics straightforward.
- Metering: we support both metered (per inference unit) and fixed-subscription SKUs. For metered SKUs we need the provider to emit usage CSVs or push events to our ingestion endpoint (we currently support S3 uploads and a simple SG webhook).
- Trials & demo entitlements: recommend a dedicated "demo-entitlement" SKU to avoid polluting production metered usage.

Attached: I'll add example mapping rows to the spreadsheet.

Sanjay — short answers from the platform side:

1) Bundled SKU: Yes. We support composite SKUs where the purchaser gets a single SKU that expands into multiple internal entitlements (runtime + support hours + optional add-ons). Operationally we model these as a primary SKU with attached sub-entitlements. For metering, sub-entitlements that are metered must be reported separately but can be aggregated on the invoice.

2) Reseller margin / private offers: For AWS Private Offers, CloudBridge receives a settlement line item if they are the reseller on the private offer. However for managed resale via CloudBridge as a partner (two-tier), we require a partner enrollment ID in the private offer metadata so the marketplace accounting routes commission correctly. If CloudBridge prefers partner invoices, we can support that workflow too but it adds manual reconciliation.
